::: {#sol-chain}

The [chain rule of probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/probability.html#thm-chain-rule) conditions each character on the ones before it:

$$\begin{aligned}
&\Pr(X_1 = \texttt{t}, X_2 = \texttt{h}, X_3 = \texttt{e}) \\
&\quad = \Pr(X_1 = \texttt{t})
\Pr(X_2 = \texttt{h} \mid X_1 = \texttt{t})
\Pr(X_3 = \texttt{e} \mid X_1 = \texttt{t}, X_2 = \texttt{h}).
\end{aligned}$$

Each factor is the probability of one character given the characters before it.
A model that gives these conditional probabilities for every string of earlier characters
gives the probability of every string.

:::
